title: Data-Efficient Conformalized Interval Prediction of Minimum Operating Voltage Capturing Process Variations
problem: Conventional Vmin prediction methods lack coverage guarantees for interval predictions. Standard Conformal Prediction predictors fail when process variations are unknown, limiting their applicability to manufacturing test scenarios.
motivation: Accurate Vmin prediction is critical for semiconductor manufacturing tests and ensuring chip reliability and yield.
method: The paper uses a statistical technique called Conformal Prediction that guarantees the true answer will fall within predicted ranges a certain percentage of the time, without needing to assume any specific probability distribution. Instead of ignoring process variations—the chip-to-chip differences that happen naturally during manufacturing—the method explicitly models them by collecting calibration data from a small set of extra chips to learn how these variations actually behave. A machine learning model then generates prediction intervals (ranges) for the minimum voltage each chip can safely operate at, with Conformal Prediction ensuring these ranges have statistically guaranteed coverage. This approach achieves both data efficiency (requiring fewer calibration chips) and rigorous statistical guarantees.
key_novelty: The key idea is applying Conformal Prediction (a statistical method that guarantees the true answer falls within the predicted range) to Vmin prediction while explicitly accounting for chip-to-chip manufacturing variations.
contributions: Application of Conformal Prediction to Vmin prediction incorporating process variation awareness
Data-efficient calibration approach requiring only a few additional chips
Rigorous coverage guarantees for interval predictions in manufacturing contexts
Validation on industrial 16nm semiconductor manufacturing data
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Data-efficient voltage prediction with statistical guarantees
